title: hybrid-async-prefetcher-with-rope-window-adaptor-for-attention-hotpath
author: Aisha R. Patel
description: Context: production workloads have hard latency tails when sequence length and request concurrency vary, and we see suboptimal KV cache warmup for prompt prefixes that oscillate between short and long tokens. Motivation: reduce 99th percentile latency and token cost by proactively prefetching KV pages and selecting an attention kernel variant that best matches the active "window" of rotary/rope offsets and batch shape. This PR introduces a hybrid async prefetcher that coordinates with a Rope Window Adaptor and the kernel selector to reduce hotpath stalls without increasing steady-state cost. What changed: introduced a new hybrid prefetcher that runs asynchronously per-serving-worker and uses a two-tier hinting mechanism (fast local hints + centralized histogram hints) to choose pages to warm in the KV cache; added Rope Window Adaptor which tracks effective rotary/rope offset distributions and exposes a compact window descriptor to the kernel selector; extended kernel_selector to consider rope window descriptors and prefetcher confidence when choosing between FlashVariantV2, FlashFallback, and tiled kernels; modified continuous_batcher to surface sequence-length histograms and per-route affinity hints to the prefetcher; updated KV cache eviction to a priority-based reservoir that prefers keeping recently-prefetched pages when prefetch confidence is high; added metrics and tagging for prefetch hits, rope-window mismatch, and kernel-choice fallbacks. Design notes: the hybrid prefetcher mixes (1) conservative, low-cost synchronous prefix warming for short requests and (2) aggressive asynchronous page prefetch for long/steady streams. The Rope Window Adaptor reduces unnecessary kernel remapping by providing a lightweight fingerprint of active rotary ranges. Kernel selection remains deterministic per-request to preserve reproducibility; the prefetcher and adaptor only influence the choice via stable hints. Compatibility & safety: changes are guarded behind a runtime flag (attn_prefetch.hybrid_enabled) and a per-tenant rollout config; fallback paths to previous behavior are retained (prefetch disabled => no change). No public API changes. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on p3/4 clusters show 18-28% reduction in 99th token latency for mixed short-long workloads and 6-10% lower token cost at 95th percentile due to fewer kernel fallback invocations; end-to-end benchmark harness (benchmarks/attn/prefetch_bench.py) included. Testing: unit tests for adaptor and selector, integration tests in sdk/python/tests/test_prefetcher.py, and stress runs on perf-canary. CI: flaky prefetch-related test fixed and retried; final CI run passed. Rollout plan: staged canary -> 25% capacity -> 100% with automatic rollback on latency regressions. Related: ENG-1245 (prefetcher design), ENG-1299 (kernel selector roadmap), SUP-212 (customer incident informing prefetch heuristics).

review_comments: Daniel Kline: The adaptor looks good but can you quantify memory overhead per worker? Suggest adding a compact delta encoding for window fingerprints.
Author (Aisha): Added compact 64-bit fingerprint representation and tracked memory in metrics; updated docs with size expectations (~48 bytes/worker average).
Marta Sokol: Kernel selector change needs a safety gate to avoid oscillation when many small requests alternate with long ones. Please add hysteresis.
Author (Aisha): Implemented 3-tier confidence hysteresis (low/medium/high) and unit tests that simulate alternating workloads.
Evan Lee: CI flake on CI/linux-asan timed out during stress test. Rerun recommended.
Author (Aisha): Investigated and fixed a race in continuous_batcher flush path; retriggered CI and all checks passed.
Marta Sokol: Approved after requested changes implemented.
Daniel Kline: LGTM, please include perf numbers in release notes.
ci_summary: Initial runs showed intermittent timeout in stress tests; fixed race and retried. Final CI: build/pass, unit tests/pass, integration tests/pass, perf-bench/job: success. No new flaky tests observed.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash on 2026-03-05. Rollout gated and monitored via perf-canary. No post-merge hotfixes necessary.
release_notes: Improves attention hotpath: introduces hybrid async prefetcher and Rope Window Adaptor to reduce 99th token latency and token cost for mixed-length workloads; adds kernel selector awareness for rope/rotary windows; configurable rollout flag attn_prefetch.hybrid_enabled.
notes_for_backport: Non-breaking runtime opt-in feature; backport candidate to release/2026-02 only if team requests prefetch on dedicated clusters. Requires careful gating and KV cache schema parity.
perf_summary: Mixed short/long workload: 18-28% 99th token latency reduction; 6-10% token-cost reduction at 95th percentile; median latency unchanged (+/-2%). Benchmarks attached in benchmarks/attn/prefetch_bench.py.
changelog_entry: runtime: add hybrid async KV prefetcher and rope window adaptor -> perf improvement for attention hotpath (ENG-1245)
additional_context: This PR complements prior kernel work by adding a scheduling/prefetch layer rather than altering attention math. It is intentionally conservative about deterministic kernel selection to avoid downstream output deltas. Operators can tune prefetch aggressiveness per-tenant.
qa_notes: To exercise: enable attn_prefetch.hybrid_enabled=true on a canary deployment and run benchmarks/attn/prefetch_bench.py using variable seq-length distribution. Monitor metrics: attn.prefetch.hits, attn.prefetch.misses, attn.rope_window.mismatch, kernel.selector.fallback_rate.
